title: Restriction kernels on a finite principal-open union commute with principal localization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $n\geq0$, and $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A$. Write $A_h=A[1/h]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $D(h)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A:h\notin\mathfrak p\}$, and put $U=\bigcup_{i=1}^nD(f_i)$. Let $K=\{a\in A:\text{the image of }a\text{ in }A_{f_i}\text{ is zero for every }i\}$. For every $g\in A$, under the section identification $\mathcal O_X(D(g))\cong A_g$ induced by restriction from $\mathcal O_X(X)=A$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b) (applied to the affine open $X$), one has the equality of subsets of $A_g$ $$\ker\bigl(\mathcal O_X(D(g))\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X(D(g)\cap U)\bigr)=\{a/g^r:a\in K,\ r\geq0\}.$$

source.place: Morphisms Tag 056C (example-scheme-theoretic-closure), the ideal I=Ker(A to product A_fi) on principal affine restrictions; Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), principal-open section and restriction identifications. The denominator calculation realizing this implicit compatibility is written in the worker report.

proof.text: Put $V=D(g)\cap U$ and $V_i=D(g)\cap D(f_i)$, so $V=\bigcup_iV_i$. The structure sheaf in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] satisfies the sheaf equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1) on the site of open subsets with open coverings. Thus a section on $V$ is zero if and only if all its restrictions to $V_i$ are zero: the section and the zero section have the same image in the product, and an equalizer map is injective. This applies also to the empty covering of the empty open.

source.place: Tag 006T (definition-sheaf), uniqueness in the sheaf axiom, including the empty covering

proof.text: Write an arbitrary section on $D(g)$ as $z=a/g^r$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b) and [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Fix $i$, and write $a_i,g_i$ for the images of $a,g$ in $A_{f_i}=\mathcal O_X(D(f_i))$. The basic open of $g_i$ in $D(f_i)$ is $V_i$: restricting a section does not change its germ at a point, so the unit-germ criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function](a) gives this equality. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b) to the affine open $D(f_i)$ and its section $g_i$. Its restriction ring on $V_i$ is $(A_{f_i})_{g_i}$, with the identification induced by restriction. Functoriality of restriction therefore sends $z$ to the image of $a_i$ times the inverse of the image of $g_i^r$: both routes send global $a,g$ to their restrictions, and ring maps preserve inverses of units. This value is zero if and only if $a_i/1=0$ in $(A_{f_i})_{g_i}$, since $g_i$ is a unit there. By the fraction equality in [def-weil-ring-localization-away], this holds if and only if $g_i^{e_i}a_i=0$ in $A_{f_i}$ for some $e_i\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), clauses (3) and (5); Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine). Fraction equality: algebra.tex, Tag 00CO (definition-localization) and preceding construction

proof.text: Suppose $z$ is in the restriction kernel. Steps 1--2 supply an exponent $e_i$ for every $i$. Take $N=\max(\{0\}\cup\{e_i:1\leq i\leq n\})$ and $b=g^Na\in A$. In $A_{f_i}$ its image is $g_i^{N-e_i}(g_i^{e_i}a_i)=0$, hence $b\in K$. In $A_g$ the fraction identity of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] gives $a/g^r=b/g^{r+N}$: the cross products $ag^{r+N}$ and $(g^Na)g^r$ are equal already in $A$. This proves inclusion in the displayed right-hand set. If $n=0$, take $N=0$; then $K=A$ and the same argument applies.

source.place: Tag 056C (example-scheme-theoretic-closure), finite principal-open kernel; explicit common-exponent calculation using algebra.tex, Tag 00CO (definition-localization)

proof.text: Conversely let $b\in K$ and $s\geq0$. Its image in each $A_{f_i}$ is zero, so Step 2, now with numerator $b$ and denominator exponent $s$, shows that $b/g^s$ restricts to zero on every $V_i$. Step 1 gives zero on $V$ itself. This proves the reverse inclusion. The zero ring and nilpotent $g$ cause no exception: the fraction relation of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and sheaf uniqueness hold for the zero ring of sections on an empty open as well.

source.place: Tag 056C (example-scheme-theoretic-closure), finite principal-open kernel; sheaves.tex Tag 006T (definition-sheaf) and algebra.tex Tag 00CO (definition-localization)
